originalTitle: US stocks: S&P closes at record high as soft jobs report eases rate-hike concerns
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a great day on Friday, with the S&P reaching its highest point ever. This happened partly because there were more job losses than expected, which made investors think that interest rates might not go up as much as they thought. This is good news for the stock market, and combined with strong earnings from companies, it helped push the market up. Additionally, oil prices went down, which helps reduce concerns about inflation, or prices rising too quickly. This all contributed to a positive day for the stock market.

originalTitle: Market cuts odds of Fed hike after jobs data, but economists still see case for tightening
simplifiedContent: Recently, the number of new jobs created in July was lower than expected, which has made investors less sure that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month. Because of this, the chances of an interest rate increase have gone down. Some officials at the Federal Reserve still think that interest rates should be raised to help control inflation, but other experts are not so sure. The Federal Reserve is paying close attention to inflation to decide what to do with interest rates in the future. This matters because interest rate changes can affect the overall economy and the stock market.

originalTitle: Dollar falls against yen, euro as weak US jobs data clouds Fed outlook
simplifiedContent: The value of the US dollar went down compared to other major currencies, like the yen and euro, on Friday. This happened because the US job market didn't do as well as expected in July, with companies cutting more jobs than anticipated. Even though the overall unemployment rate got a little better, fewer people were working or looking for work, which is a concern. This news makes it less clear what the Federal Reserve (the group that controls interest rates) will do next. As a result, people are less confident in the US dollar, which is why its value decreased.

originalTitle: Short-Term Treasuries Cap Biggest Weekly Rally Since May on Data
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the value of short-term US government bonds (called Treasuries) went up a lot this week. This happened because a recent report on employment in the US was weaker than expected, which made investors think that the Federal Reserve (the central bank of the US) might not raise interest rates as much as they thought. As a result, the value of these bonds had their biggest weekly increase since May. This matters because it shows that investors are changing their expectations about what the Federal Reserve will do with interest rates, which can affect the overall economy. The increase in value is a significant move, indicating a shift in investor sentiment.

originalTitle: Treasury yields fall as jobs report dashes hike bets
simplifiedContent: The US government released a report about jobs, and it had an impact on the stock market. This report made investors think that interest rates might not go up as much as they thought, which caused "Treasury yields" to decrease. Treasury yields are like interest rates on loans that the US government gives to itself, and when they go down, it can affect the whole economy. This change happened because the jobs report wasn't as strong as some people expected, which made them less sure that interest rates would increase. As a result, the value of Treasury yields fell, which can have a ripple effect on other investments.

originalTitle: Gold hits seven-week high as weak US jobs data dents rate hike bets
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has reached its highest point in seven weeks. This happened because a recent report on US jobs was weaker than expected, which made investors think that interest rates might not increase as quickly as they thought. As a result, people are buying more gold, which is causing its price to go up. This matters because it shows how investors are reacting to economic news and making decisions about where to put their money. The change in gold's price is a sign that investors are less sure about the economy and are looking for safer investments.
